full_judgment:
8. The learned Assistant Attorney-General appearing for the State supports the impugned judgment contending, inter alia, that in the facts of the case and the evidence on record, the learned Sessions Judge was fully justified in passing the impugned order of conviction and sentence against the accused appellants. 

 10. We have gone through the first information report of the case, charges framed against the accused-persons at the trial, the evidence of the prosecution witnesses as well as the impugned judgment. We are now called upon to consider the legality and propriety of the impugned judgment in the light of the evidence on record. 

 11. PW 1 informant Khaleda Khatoon, sister of deceased Mosleuddin, fully corroborated the case made out in the first information report. She stated in her evidence that deceased Mosleuddin came to her house at about evening time on 21st Magh, 1391 BS. At that time her 1st cousin accused Majibur Rahman and Bachchu came there and took away Mosleuddin with them on the plea of bringing back their lost cow from village Charbhelamari and since then Mosleuddin is not traceable. On the next morning PW 3 Noor Hossain told her that the dead body of Musleuddin was lying near the ditch of one Rahim Fakir at Charlakhidia. Immediately thereafter informant Khaleda Khatoon with her husband and other relations went to the scene and found the dead body of Mosleuddin with injuries on it. She disclosed to the people present there that on the previous evening accused Bachchu and Mojibur Rahman had called away deceased Mosleuddin from her house on the plea of bringing back their lost cow from village Char Sreerampur and Mosleuddin did not return. She strongly suspected that the accused-persons had killed her brother Mosleuddin due to enmity over landed properties. She lodged the first information report Exhibit 3 at Nandail Police Station. 

 27. From the discussion of the evidence made above, it is found that there is no eye-witness to the occurrence. No other witness except informant Khaleda Khatoon saw deceased Mosleuddin going away with accused Mujibur Rahman and Bachchu for searching out the lost cow of the accused persons from Charbhelamari. There is no evidence on record to establish that the cow of the accused persons was lost and it could be available at village Charbhelamari. So, the whole prosecution case hinges on the solitary evidence of informant Khaleda Khatoon in taking away deceased Mosleuddin by accused Mujibur Rahman and Bachchu from the house on the false plea of recovery of their lost cow. It is an admitted fact that there existed land dispute between the parties. It is true that the prosecution tried to introduce a new story in the case by giving out that about 8/10 days prior to the occurrence the dispute between the parties was amicably settled so as to give an impression that because of the new development in the relationships between the parties it might be possible for deceased Mosleuddin to accompany accused Bachchu and Mujibur Rahman for searching out their missing cow. This appears to be a clear embellishment. In such circumstances, it is difficult to place explicit reliance on the evidence of PW 1 Khaleda Khatoon and to act on it. Moreover, deceased Mosleuddin was allegedly called away from the house of PW 2 Khaleda Khatoon at about evening time. Nobody knows what happened to him during the whole right following the deceitful abduction of deceased Mosleuddin by the accused-persons. In the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence on record, we are of the view that the prosecution has not been able to prove the guilt of the accused-appellants by adducing cogent and reliable evidence. 

 28. The law on circumstantial evidence is well settled by now. When there exists a well-knit and unbroken chain of circumstances leading to the inevitable conclusion that none but the accused committed the alleged offence and no other hypothesis other than the guilt of the accused can be inferred from the given circumstances, a conviction can be safely based on circumstantial evidence alone. But the facts and circumstances of the present case fall far short of the standard requirement for safely basing an order of conviction on the untidy and almost stray evidence of informant Khaleda Khatoon. The evidence adduced by the prosecution in the case can at best provide suspicion against the accused, but suspicion howsoever high and probable can never take the place of legal evidence. 

 29. We have given our anxious consideration to the facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence on record but we fail to persuade ourselves to subscribe to the view taken by the learned Sessions Judge. We are therefore, constrained to hold that the prosecution failed to prove its case against the accused-appellants beyond reasonable doubts and they are entitled to acquittal accordingly. The appeal succeeds.
